items.title: US soldier killed and one injured after Iranian attack in Iraq
items.description: The US military reports another death a day after two of its soldiers were killed in Jordan.

items.title: Tate brothers arrested in US as further UK charges take total to 59
items.description: The Crown Prosecution Service says it has requested their extradition from the US, while their lawyer says they are innocent.

items.title: Russia launches major ballistic missile attack on Ukrainian cities
items.description: Eight people die and dozens are injured as several cities are hit by missile and drone attacks, while Kyiv continues its own assault on Russian infrastructure.

items.title: New EU border system tripling time at passport control, airport boss says
items.description: Ryanair has also warned passengers travelling to Europe this summer to prepare for extended waits.

items.title: The 1975's Matty Healy marries model Gabbriette Bechtel in Los Angeles
items.description: The newlyweds were first linked in 2023 after Healy's brief relationship with Taylor Swift.

items.title: Ferry carrying 133 passengers and crew sinks off Guyana coast
items.description: Fifteen children are among 67 people rescued, officials say, with dozens still missing.

items.title: Health officials identify source of US explosive diarrhoea outbreak
items.description: The US Food and Drug Administration says iceberg lettuce supplied by Taylor Farms and sold at Taco Bell and Walmart locations was the source of cyclosporiasis infections.

items.title: Neighbours actor Terence Donovan dies aged 90
items.description: His son, actor Jason Donovan, posted to social media that his father died on Saturday night peacefully in Melbourne, Australia

items.title: Cuban dissident Luis Manuel Otero Alcántara goes into exile in US
items.description: He was arrested in 2021 during Cuba's largest anti-government protests in decades and spent five years ⁠in prison.

items.title: Runners complete 'world's coolest marathon' on drifting North Pole ice
items.description: Organisers say 23 runners from seven countries took part in races at the Arctic's geographic North Pole.

items.title: Hungary's president agrees to stand down after parliament backs removal
items.description: Tamás Sulyok, seen as an Orbán loyalist, had until Saturday night to agree to end his term.

items.title: German politician resigns over surrogacy child controversy
items.description: Jens Spahn faced criticism over his use of a surrogate, a ban on which he previously backed.
